newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - March 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - March 20.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- GERMAN STEEL MERGER TALKS EASE BID FEAR

Krupp and Thyssen, two of Germany's largest industrial companies agreed on Wednesday to hold talks about scaling down the merger of their steel operations, bowing to political concerns about heavy job losses in the industrialised Ruhr region. Krupp, which had announced a 5 billion pounds stg bid for its larger rival Thyssen on Tuesday, said it would drop the takeover if the two companies could agree to merge their steel businesses within eight days.
-- VICKERS ISSUES WARNINGS DESPITE LEAP TO 83 MILLION POUNDS

Vickers, maker of Rolls-Royce cars and Challenger tanks, posted warnings about its profit and sales outlook this year, causing its shares to slump on Wednesday. Pre-tax profits were up 11 percent last year to 83.3 million pounds stg, but Vickers claims that the strength of sterling make it unusually difficult to predict sales and earnings this year. The share price ended Wednesday down 22p to 239p.
-- BEAZER PROFIT UP BUT BUILDERS SHORT OF MANPOWER

Beazer Group reported a 28 percent rise in interim pre-tax profits to 23.8 million pounds stg on Wednesday but warned that Britain's housebuilders are facing the worst skill shortages in 10 years. A sharp upturn on the housing market has stretched the labour pool, causing problems in recruiting sub-contract employees.
THE TIMES
-- JOBLESS RATE DECLINES TO SIX-YEAR LOW

The UK unemployment rate fell for the 12th consecutive month, taking the total drop over the past year to 466,000. The government claimed on Wednesday that Britain's economic situation is now excellent following the news of a fall of 68,200 in the number of jobless. The Office for National Statistics said the figures were still being affected by the replacement of Unemployment Benefit by the Jobseekers' Allowance.
-- KINGFISHER TO EXPAND IN ASIA AS PROFITS JUMP

Retail conglomerate Kingfisher has announced plans to open two new branches of B&Q, the do-it-yourself market leader, in Taiwan. Chief executive Sir Geoffrey Mulcahy believes the new branches would lead to greater understanding of the Asian market and possibly to the opening of its other formats there, including Woolworths, Comet and Superdrug.
-- B&B PLANS DOUBLING OF BENEFITS TO 100 MILLION POUNDS

Bradford & Bingley, the building society, lifted its battle against converting societies on Wednesday, promising to double its members' benefits scheme to 100 million pounds stg this year. From March to December 1996, the society returned 43 million pounds stg to members in the form of improved savings and mortgage rates.
THE GUARDIAN
-- RATE RISE RISK BOOSTS POUND

City expectations of a post-election interest rate rise strengthened on Wednesday as the pound rose sharply on foreign exchanges due to falling unemployment, rising earnings growth and buoyant high street sales. Dealers marked up sterling by over two pfennigs against the German mark as speculation intensified that the cost of borrowing would be increased by a Labour or Conservative government at the monthly monetary meeting on May 7.
-- NORWICH POLICYHOLDERS GET SURPRISE SHARE ISSUE

Norwich Union is expected to announce on Thursday that it will offer free shares worth between 600 and 800 pounds stg for its three million with-profits policyholders when it floats on the stock market in the summer. The converting mutual insurer is expected also to announce that it will include non-with-profits policyholders in the bonanza with each receiving 150 shares, worth somewhere between 300 and 400 pounds stg.
-- RENAULT BATTLE BACK TO STREETS

Workers at Renault pledged on Wednesday night to step up industrial action across Europe after failing to reverse planned job cuts. Following a four-hour meeting with trade union representatives at Beauvais, northern France, Renault refused to go back on its decision to close the company's plant at Vilvorde, three weeks ago.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- CABLE & WIRELESS EDGES CLOSER TO US PARTNERSHIP

Speculation is growing that Cable & Wireless has moved closer to a long awaited partnership with Sprint of the US. Although Cable & Wireless refused to comment on reports that it was examining a takeover bid for Sprint, the US's third-largest long distance phone operator, analysts see it as the logical way for C&W to ally itself with Global One, the alliance between the US company and its partners France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom. The move could closely follow BT's planned 13 billion merger with MCI.
-- REXAM TO AXE 1,200 STAFF

Packaging group Rexam announced on Wednesday that 1,200 jobs would be cut alongside 190 million pounds stg of losses, as new management attempts to overcome past mistakes. New chairman Jeremy Lancaster said the job cuts and exceptional charges amounting to 358 million pounds stg resulted from the decision to take action over underperformance of businesses, by making disposals and removing excess capacity.
-- CO-OP HIRES TOP MERCHANT BANKER TO FIGHT LANCIA

The Co-operative Movement hired Brian Keelan of SBC Warburg, one of the City's top merchant bankers, to represent it as part of its defence against Lancia Trust's takeover bid. The appointment on Wednesday came as a group of almost 50 Labour MPs put down an Early Day Motion denouncing Lancia's Andrew Regan as an "asset stripper".
